deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the opening sheet ('Riemann 18', archive no. 104) of Riemann's fragment on gravitation and light. The heading reads 'a, Bewegung, welche die Gravitationserscheinungen verursacht'. Section b on the next page, about light propagation, sets up a variational principle for an aether in which U plays the role of the gravitational potential. This page states the static potential-theoretic laws that the later aether model must reproduce.

(i) The components of gravity parallel to the axes are F_i = ∂V/∂x_i for a function V of position, the potential function. Experience, through the general laws of motion, determines V only up to an additive term that is constant in space (Riemann's struck phrase 'abgesehen von einer ... Function' means a function not depending on the coordinates).

(ii) Uniqueness conditions. V is completely determined if:
- it is not discontinuous across a surface;
- ∫ΔV dx1dx2dx3 is nonzero only in a finite region;
- the boundary condition is replaced by the decay condition R·∂V/∂x_i → 0 as R → ∞, where R is the distance from the points of that region.

(iii) Empirical law. ΔV·dx1dx2dx3 = 0 outside ponderable bodies. For each ponderable element it equals −4π times the mass (absolute attracting strength) assigned to it. In modern form this is Poisson's equation ΔV = −4πρ, with V = ∫ρ/r dτ and force +∇V; the sign convention is correct.

(iv) Uniqueness argument (fragmentary). Suppose two solutions V', V'' exist and set W = V' − V''. Then ΔW = 0 everywhere, W is continuous, and R∇W → 0. Riemann considers the Dirichlet integral ∫|∇W|² dτ. By Green's identity (my filling-in) it equals a surface term at infinity, which he takes to vanish. Hence ∇W = 0 and W = const, so V' − V'' = 0 up to the irrelevant constant. He also remarks, mostly struck out, that one must prove a function satisfying the laws always exists. This is an allusion to the existence problem (Dirichlet principle) and to the notion of a continuous derivative.

(v) Reformulation in first-order form. Write u_i for the candidate force components, so that 'by our hypothesis ∂V/∂x_i = u_i' and dV = u1dx1 + u2dx2 + u3dx3. The laws become:
(1) ∂u2/∂x3 − ∂u3/∂x2 = 0, ∂u3/∂x1 − ∂u1/∂x3 = 0, ∂u1/∂x2 − ∂u2/∂x1 = 0, i.e. curl u = 0;
(2) (∂u1/∂x1 + ∂u2/∂x2 + ∂u3/∂x3) dx1dx2dx3 = −4π dm, i.e. div u = −4πρ.

Claim: u equals the gravitational force whenever it satisfies (1) and (2), is continuous, matter occupies a finite region, and R·u_i → 0.

Proof sketch given: (1) guarantees the existence of a function U with ∂U/∂x_i = u_i, i.e. dU = Σu_i dx_i is exact (the space is simply connected; this is my addition). (2) and the decay condition then make U satisfy the same conditions as V, so U = V by step (iv).

A struck/garbled passage mentions 'Geschwindigkeitscomponenten' (velocity components). This suggests Riemann already intends to interpret the u_i as velocity components of a medium, which is carried out on the next page.
errors: The energy (Dirichlet-integral) argument for uniqueness is not justified by the stated decay condition alone. From R|∇W| → 0 one only gets W = o(log R), so the surface term ∮W ∂W/∂n dS over a sphere of radius R is o(R log R), which need not vanish. The conclusion is nevertheless true: the components of ∇W are harmonic and tend to 0, so by Liouville/the maximum principle ∇W ≡ 0. Riemann's sketch leaves this gap.

The passage from curl u = 0 to the existence of U tacitly assumes simple connectivity of the domain (whole space here, so harmless) and differentiability of u. Point masses (dm as genuine points) would make u singular; Riemann's continuity assumption implicitly means distributed mass.
Determinacy is only up to an additive constant. Riemann acknowledges this in (i), but writes V' − V'' = 0 in (iv) without restating the normalization.

results.what: Gravity force is the gradient of a potential function V (named 'Potentialfunction')
results.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (1773), Laplace (1782); term 'potential function' Green (1828), Gauss (1840)

results.what: Uniqueness of the potential given ΔV and decay R∇V → 0, via the Dirichlet integral
results.modern_name: Uniqueness theorem for Poisson's equation in R^3 (energy method)

results.what: Field u with curl u = 0, div u = −4πρ, decaying at infinity, equals the gravitational force; curl-free implies gradient
results.modern_name: Div–curl characterization of a vector field (special case of the Helmholtz decomposition theorem)

results.what: Static gravitational laws prepared for interpretation as velocity field of an aether (continued on next page)
results.modern_name: Riemann's aether theory of gravitation and light (fragment 'Gravitation und Licht')

deep.surprise_reason: The page is standard potential theory: gradient potential, Poisson equation, uniqueness by energy method, and curl/div characterization. It forms the preamble to Riemann's known and published fragment on gravitation and light. Nothing here goes beyond what Green, Gauss, Dirichlet and Helmholtz had; the only interest is as context for his aether program, which is already known.

checkable.asserts: Laplacian of 1/r is 0 away from the origin (ΔV = 0 outside matter)

checkable.asserts: Flux of grad(1/r) through a sphere is −4π, giving the −4π dm in Poisson's law

checkable.asserts: Conditions (1): a gradient field has vanishing curl

transcription_corrections: Heading likely reads 'a, Bewegung, welche die Gravitationserscheinungen verursacht' rather than 'Erzeugung, welche eine ...', parallel to 'b, Bewegungen, welche die Lichtausbreitung verursacht' on the next page.
'Nach unserer Hypothese ist nun ∂U/∂x = u' should read ∂V/∂x = u, since the following line is dV = u1dx1 + u2dx2 + u3dx3. U appears only later, as the function whose existence follows from (1).
'Stücke des Raumes' belongs to the phrase 'außerhalb eines endlichen Stückes des Raumes', i.e. ΔV is nonzero only in a finite region.
The uniqueness integral is ∫Σ(∂(V'−V'')/∂x)² dx1dx2dx3, summed over the three coordinates.
'(104)' is the archive folio number, not part of the text.
